another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

I can see you live in the UK and are asking about Child Benefit for Alex, who is 11 years old and lives with you. Let me gather a bit more information to make a complete assessment.

I need to ask you one important question:

**Is there anyone else living with Alex who might also claim Child Benefit for them?** (For example, another parent, partner, or guardian?) 

This is important because only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child, and I need to understand if there's anyone else who might have a competing claim.

Thank you. Based on the information provided in your situation profile, I now have sufficient details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the key facts:
- You live in the UK
- Alex is 11 years old (under 16)
- Alex lives with you
- Alex is not in local authority care, hospital, or residential accommodation
- Alex is not fostered
- Alex does not work 24+ hours/week
- Alex has not started an apprenticeship
- Alex does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

According to the UK Child Benefit rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK. You'll usually be responsible for a child if you live with them.

Alex meets all the eligibility criteria: they are under 16, live with you in the UK, and none of the disqualifying circumstances apply (not in care, not working full-time, etc.).

The only unknown factor is whether another person living with Alex might have priority for claiming, but this would be a matter for you and that person to decide between yourselves, or for HMRC to determine if you cannot agree. It doesn't make you ineligible - it just means only one person can claim.

## Good News! You Are Eligible for Child Benefit

**For Alex:** ✓ **ELIGIBLE**

You meet all the requirements for claiming Child Benefit for Alex because:
- You live in the UK
- Alex is 11 years old (under 16)
- Alex lives with you, which means you're responsible for them
- None of the disqualifying circumstances apply

### Next Steps

You can apply for Child Benefit for Alex. Remember that only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child, so if anyone else (such as another parent or guardian living with Alex) also wants to claim, you'll need to agree between yourselves who will make the claim.

### Important Note About High Income

Be aware that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can still claim Child Benefit, but you might need to pay some or all of it back through your tax return.

If you have any other questions about claiming Child Benefit, feel free to ask!
